booster-apps-seo-optimizer.text: Strongly recommend avoiding this app if you use Shopify Markets or care about your SEO. The app does not clearly explain that it is not properly designed for a multi-market setup, and the way it modifies theme code can create serious problems. In our case, after uninstalling the app, it left behind code overrides that continued interfering with Shopify’s native SEO. Worse, the uninstall did not properly restore the original theme code. Our native page titles and meta descriptions had been commented out, which caused major SEO issues across product pages, collection pages, and other parts of the site. Titles were no longer being handled correctly, and in some cases URLs were effectively being used where proper titles should have been. We had to manually go into the Shopify theme code, disable the leftover Booster SEO include, and remove the comment tags around Shopify’s original title and meta-description code just to get the store functioning normally again. An app should never leave behind code that continues to override critical SEO settings after it has been uninstalled. At the very least, the developer should clearly warn merchants about this behavior and provide a proper cleanup process. If you use Shopify Markets, multiple countries, languages, or domains, be extremely careful with this app. Uninstalling it does not necessarily undo the changes it made.

It's not ideal if you have markets in different languages. There needs to be a way to adjust the SEO, for example, the titles, etc., to be adapted to each market in language and not just be based off of the primary language or market.

1/5 — FOUR YEARS OF BUILDING A PREMIUM BRAND PUT AT RISK. ABSOLUTELY NOT RECOMMENDED. As the founder and owner of Ewa Mrochen Jewellery®, an independent premium jewellery brand that I have spent four years passionately building on Shopify, I consider my experience with Booster SEO absolutely unacceptable. Four years of dedication, creative work, financial investment, brand development, customer trust and meticulous attention to detail deserve to be treated with respect. Instead, after installing Booster SEO and paying $69 per month for its premium plan, I discovered extensive, unwanted modifications across my online store. These included: * Changes to product and page URLs. * Automatically generated ALT text that frequently failed to accurately describe my jewellery. * Unwanted modifications to SEO metadata. * Problematic changes involving links and other store resources. * Significant additional work identifying, reviewing and correcting these changes manually. This was not the professional SEO optimisation service I believed I was paying for. It was a deeply damaging experience for a business I had spent four years building. What makes this situation even more disappointing is my experience with customer support and the lack of satisfactory accountability for the problems I reported. Paying $69 per month for a premium service creates reasonable expectations of competent technical assistance, transparency, responsible handling of customer concerns and effective solutions. My experience fell far below those expectations. The lack of adequate Polish-language support was another disappointment for a business operating in Poland. I entrusted this application with access to an established Shopify store representing years of independent creative work. Instead of confidently focusing on my customers, new collections and business development, I found myself spending valuable time investigating and correcting unwanted changes. An SEO application should protect and strengthen a business’s digital foundations, not leave its owner questioning the integrity of years of work. To the developers: behind every Shopify store is a real business, real financial investment, real customers and often years of someone’s life. That responsibility should never be taken lightly. To fellow Shopify entrepreneurs worldwide: please exercise extreme caution before granting this application access to your store. Review its permissions, document your existing SEO settings and closely monitor every automated change. My experience has completely destroyed my trust in this service. ONE STAR. ABSOLUTELY NOT RECOMMENDED. Ewa Mrochen Jewellery® | ewamrochen.com

One star. I engaged with two support agents, Lina and later Florence. Lina stopped responding for extended periods, resulting in a chat that lasted nearly an hour solely because of prolonged response times. The issue itself was not complex, but the lack of timely communication made it impossible to proceed. By the time Florence intervened, I was already preparing to exit due to the delays. Lina made several statements that were incorrect, contradictory, and misleading. She stated that the bots “won’t hurt anything,” despite the fact that they were actively affecting my analytics and abandoned checkout data. She also stated that “blocking is not foolproof” and the app may or may not work because bots can change their IP addresses. This directly undermines the fundamental purpose of a security and bot-prevention solution. Her claim that the free plan is primarily for “exploring” features rather than actually using them contradicts the way the app is marketed and creates a misleading expectation for new users. Florence later reiterated the same limitations and added that DNS-level blocking, a critical security function, is still “in testing” and not available. This indicates that essential protection mechanisms are incomplete or not fully operational, regardless of whether a merchant is on a free or paid plan. For a security-focused app, this represents a significant reliability concern. After uninstalling the app, I immediately received back-to-back emails from Florence containing shifting explanations. Additionally, within thirty minutes of the initial installation, I was already receiving promotional emails from Blockify. The frequency, timing, and volume of these emails felt excessive and spam-like. As a small business owner, this experience was profoundly disappointing. Security tools must be dependable, transparent, and functional upon installation. Hearing directly from support that the app is “not foolproof” and may or may not work—even on paid tiers—raises serious concerns about reliability, consistency, and product readiness. Anything less than stable, predictable performance becomes a costly waste of time and resources. I strongly encourage prospective users to review the one-star feedback as well as comments from long-term users who have relied on this app for over a year. The recurring themes in those reviews reflect the same support, performance, and reliability issues I encountered.

**What worked well:** * **Intuitive bulk-editor interface**: Picking a tag filter and choosing “Set text to value” is straightforward. * **Accurate preview and reporting**: The app clearly shows which SKUs you’ve “edited” and gives confirmation messages. * **General metafield support**: I could bulk-set other custom fields without issue. **Where it fell short:** * **Google Shopping fields not updating**: Although the app reported success, the values never appeared in the **Google Shopping – Custom Label 0/1** metafields. * **Lack of namespace clarity**: It wasn’t obvious whether “Custom Label 0” referred to Shopify metafields or Google-channel fields, leading to confusion. * **No visible error**: There’s no warning when a write operation silently fails on the `google_shopping.custom_label_*` namespace. **Suggested improvements:** 1. **Explicit Google-Shopping field mapping**: Clearly label fields with the full namespace (`google_shopping.custom_label_0`) and surface it in the bulk-editor. 2. **Error reporting**: If a write to a Google-channel metafield fails, show an error or flag it in the preview. 3. **Sample verification**: Offer a “Verify in Google channel” step so I can confirm values made it into Merchant Center fields. I approved the \$30 plan hoping to streamline Google feed prep, but since custom labels didn’t actually update, it wasn’t usable for our biggest use case. If you can address the above points, I’d be happy to give Ablestar another try!

If you have a simple store with a few products, perhaps this app works. But if you manage dozens of products with complex options and depend on accurate pricing, be extremely careful. Pricing would not display correctly, repeated patches were required, and after support began making changes, we started finding incorrect pricing and problems across other products. We have spent days troubleshooting and repairing issues and have finally given up. Something we wish we had understood beforehand: once you commit to Easify, getting out is not as simple as uninstalling the app. We are now manually rebuilding dozens of options back into Shopify. Most concerning, shortly after granting Easify's support team access to our store, an entire product page disappeared along with images from our library. We continue to discover additional missing images. We cannot confirm what caused this, but the timing is concerning enough that we have opened an investigation with Shopify to determine what happened. One final piece of advice: don't just focus on all the positive reviews. Read the negative reviews first. Look at the problems other merchants have experienced and then decide whether you are still comfortable trusting the app with your store. We wish we had paid considerably more attention to those reviews before committing. After 5 years of building our Shopify store, this has been one of the most frustrating app experiences we have had. We did request a refund for our purchase since we started to encountered major issues. We keep track of time spend correcting software issues and the hours spend on our overhead account attributed to Easify issues was at $1,473.00CAD as of today. Not worth paying $10 extra a month. **Overall, this app does a lot. It has a lot of great features that you cant usually find all in 1 app. But there are a ton of hang-ups that make my job harder. I am actively looking for other solutions but this app is our best option for now.

Easify is a great app when it works, but unfortunately, that is the main issue. When it works, it does a lot of what we need and the live support can be helpful for smaller changes, such as adjusting text styling, aesthetics, and minor display issues. However, there are some important features missing that make the app frustrating to use at scale. The live preview feature is quite limited. You can only have one live preview option working properly, and if you add another live preview option, it can break the first one. For stores that rely heavily on visual customisation, this is a big limitation. The template feature also is not as useful as it could be. At the moment, you can only create a single option template, rather than a full option set template with multiple options inside it. This makes it harder to manage products efficiently, especially when you have a large catalogue. Another major issue is that you cannot add a new option to every product with one click. For example, if you wanted to add a new option to 100 different products, you would have to manually go into each product and add it individually. This could be massively improved with an option set priority system, where higher priority option sets appear above lower priority ones on the product page. That way, you could assign a new option set to hundreds of products, give it a lower priority, and have it automatically appear underneath the existing product options. The most frustrating issue, though, is that the app randomly breaks. At least once a month, we have to contact Easify support because something that was working perfectly fine suddenly stops working, despite us changing nothing. As I am writing this, Easify has completely disappeared from our store. Customers currently cannot purchase products because the app is not working. We also have another store where Easify is working fine, which makes it feel like the issue is specific to our main store. Honestly, we are exhausted from dealing with the constant problems. Our whole website depends on Easify, and moving to another app would take hundreds of hours because of the number of products we have set up. So while the app has great potential and can be very useful when it works, the reliability issues make it incredibly stressful to depend on for a live business.

This led to orders going through with €0 extra — a critical bug that caused real financial loss. 2. Confirmed performance drop (before/after tests) We ran multiple Lighthouse audits before and after uninstalling the app: • Product page (desktop): went from 46 → 95 • Product page (mobile): 22 → 46 • Home page (desktop): 63 → 74 • Home page (mobile): 85 → 95 These results were consistent across several runs. No other change was made between the tests besides removing Easify — which confirms the app had a measurable impact on page speed. 3. Limited dev availability despite “24/7 support” While replies were polite and courteous, basic questions like “Where is tracking configured?” or “How to fully uninstall?” could not be answered in real time. We were told the dev team would respond in 6–10 hours, due to their time zone. This does not meet the expectations of true 24/7 technical support — especially for stores based in Europe. Final response from Easify They confirmed the app uses Shopify’s extension system, does not inject tracking scripts, and that no manual cleanup is needed after uninstall. That’s appreciated — but came too late, after real losses and slowdowns. ⸻ Summary: The app has potential, but for us, it caused lost revenue, degraded performance, and long delays in support. It may be suitable for simple setups, but if your store is sensitive to speed and operational stability, use with caution.

pagefly.text: Updated Review — Excellent Legacy Editor, Disappointing Gen 2 Experience I originally left PageFly a very positive review after using its legacy editor to build and customize our Wallhogs website nearly 9 years ago. At the time, I found it intuitive, flexible, and well-designed, with clearly labeled controls that made creating custom layouts relatively straightforward. Unfortunately, my experience with PageFly Gen 2 while building another Shopify website has been considerably different. As an experienced website designer with a background in the e-commerce industry, I find the new Flex Block-based editor unnecessarily restrictive and cumbersome compared with the legacy version. Many of the tools and controls that made the original editor so effective have either been removed, reorganized, or replaced with less intuitive alternatives. The right-hand settings panel is particularly frustrating. Controls have been renamed or grouped in ways that make their functions difficult to understand, and there is little contextual guidance explaining what they actually do. The learning curve has increased substantially, even for someone already familiar with PageFly. Responsive design has also become unnecessarily complicated. Tasks such as aligning images of different proportions within a three-column layout now require manual adjustments across multiple device breakpoints. Even more concerning, I've encountered instances where layouts display correctly in the Gen 2 editor but render differently on the published Shopify storefront. The legacy editor allowed me to concentrate on designing the website. Gen 2 frequently forces me to concentrate on figuring out how to operate the editor. I still believe PageFly's original product was excellent, which makes this redesign particularly disappointing. I hope the development team seriously considers restoring the flexibility, intuitive controls, clear labeling, and designer-focused functionality that made the legacy editor so effective. At this point, I would be reluctant to use Gen 2 for another custom website project.

Support is happy to fix them, but even upon request I've never gotten a straight answer about why they happen in the first place. It seems every time the app is updated things across existing pages break... or just randomly. 2. This is the biggy - on more than one occasion support has responded to one of these bug inquires with a "fix" that has broken major components of our site. Most recently they fixed an image link glitch and published the page to the wrong URL, so all links to the page (our primary selling page) went to a 404 error. Whatever code they added also broke the Add to Cart functionality across our entire site, so no customers could add any products to the cart to place orders. Their devs made these changes overnight and published them live, without consulting with me or my team, and obviously without proper QA. Again, the app really is very feature rich and flexible, I had originally chosen it after reviewing several others - but these types of issues have cost us a ton of frustration, time and revenue, and I just can't continue to take that risk.
